content.overview: Propagation output becomes usable only when the receiving team can verify what arrived, what was excluded, what remains uncertain and who owns follow-up. Improvement depends on closing that loop.

vocabulary.definition: Transfer of identified material, records, status and responsibility between controlled process stages or teams.
An authorized action addressing a demonstrated cause or control failure, with follow-up verification.

sections.title: Reconcile physical and recorded quantity
sections.body: The handoff should match counts, cultivar or accession, batch, stage, status and destination. Discrepancies are resolved or explicitly transferred as exceptions.

sections.title: Communicate exceptions without hiding uncertainty
sections.body: Slow lines, partial releases, holds, damage and unusual treatment history should travel with the material. The receiver should not need to infer risk from plant appearance.

sections.title: Improvement closes with verification
sections.body: A corrective action is incomplete until its implementation and effect are checked. Trend review should distinguish one-time recovery from sustained process change.

workedExamples: A partial release lists the original cohort, released units, held units, reasons and next review owner.
A revised sanitation step is verified across subsequent batches before the deviation is considered closed.
commonMistakes: Handing off plants without exception history.
Closing an action when it is assigned rather than verified.
content.practicalApplication: Prepare a complete handoff for a mixed-status propagation cohort and a 30-day follow-up plan that verifies whether the selected corrective action changed the intended metric.
content.summary: A strong handoff reconciles identity, quantity, status and exceptions, then connects corrective action to follow-up evidence.
